issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (see problem_statement.md), but both the template and the solution use the method name singFarmSong() in Farm.java. This name mismatch in the API described vs. provided will confuse students about which method to implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either change the problem statement to instruct students to implement singFarmSong(), or add a printFarmSong() method in the template/solution that delegates to singFarmSong() (e.g., public void printFarmSong() { singFarmSong(); }). Ensure tests and documentation refer to the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) refers to a public method named printFarmSong() to play the song, but both the provided template and the solution implement and expect a method named singFarmSong(). This cross-artifact method-name mismatch (printFarmSong vs. singFarmSong) can confuse students: the instructions tell them to implement printFarmSong(), yet the starter code and final implementation use singFarmSong(), making it unclear which identifier to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to reference singFarmSong() everywhere, or (B) rename the public method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong(). Ensure Main, tests (if any), and documentation are updated to use the same method name.
